record.title: The UI and CLI audit timelines stop at the 5000th row, so an agent can push its later actions out of the human's view
record.description: The sandbox page's audit fragment (GET /ui/audit, re-polled every 3 s) and `agentbox audit` both fetch rows with AuditLog.list(limit=5000) and no after_id. AuditLog.list is `WHERE id > ? [AND sandbox_id = ?] ORDER BY id LIMIT ?`, so it returns the OLDEST 5000 matching rows, and nothing is ever pruned. Once a sandbox (sandbox page, `agentbox audit --sandbox`) or the whole system (default `agentbox audit`) holds more than 5000 rows, the UI shows the last 400 of the oldest window (ids 4601-5000, total capped at 5000) and the CLI prints rows 1-5000. Every later row (tool_request/tool_result, snapshot, human_takeover/handback, gui_processes_stopped, gui_changes) is never shown, while the UI footer keeps saying it shows the most recent 400 of 5000. The UI window is per sandbox; the default CLI view is system-wide, so one sandbox's volume also hides other sandboxes' later events from it. A prompt-injected agent that holds only its own sandbox's agent token can reach the threshold without any approval: one approval_forbidden row per refused POST /approvals/{any id} (no Docker, no rate limit; needs raw API access with the token), or three rows per allowed tool call such as list_dir or exec of an allowlisted read-only command (about 1,670 calls through the ordinary MCP tools). Correction to the hunter's example: `exec true` is not an approval-free path, because default_policy.yaml lists true/false unquoted (line 27) and PyYAML parses them as booleans, so that call returns 202 and needs approval; `exec ls`, `exec echo` and list_dir are allowed. Long-lived ordinary sandboxes reach the same threshold without any attacker. The rows stay in the database, GET /audit?after_id=... returns them, verify passes and the approval queue is unaffected; only the two views humans actually use stop updating.
record.root_cause: AuditLog.list (audit.py:190-197) can only return the oldest `limit` rows after `after_id` (ORDER BY id ascending). Both human-facing consumers call it with limit=5000 and no after_id and then treat the result as the newest window: web.py audit_frag takes rows[-400:] and total=len(rows), and cli.py cmd_audit prints the whole list. Beyond 5000 rows the 'tail' is the tail of the oldest 5000, never the newest rows, and total is capped at 5000. Neither the UI nor the CLI has a paging control and the audit table is never pruned, so the freeze is permanent for that sandbox or system.
record.intended_behavior: The sandbox page timeline (footer: only the most recent N shown, total M) and `agentbox audit` show the newest audit events with the real total, or page through all rows. The volume of rows an agent can create must not hide its later events from the human's oversight views, in particular the gui_changes and gui_processes_stopped records that the README (line 198) names as the way the human sees changes made through the ungated GUI path.

trace.description: An agent token (lowest-trust principal) calling POST /approvals/{any id} with a valid {"decision": ...} body is authenticated by principal() and refused with 403, but the refusal path records an audit row first. Ordinary allowed tool calls (POST /sandboxes/{sid}/tools/{tool}: list_dir, read_file, exec of an allowlisted command, GUI tools) also add rows, three each via service.py:297, 305 and 359.

audit.append(actor='agent', event='approval_forbidden', sandbox_id=p.sandbox_id): one row per request, tagged with the agent's own sandbox id. No request-rate limit (none in the app or in deploy/), no tool_pool slot, no Docker call and no row cap; tool_concurrency only bounds simultaneous tool calls.

'WHERE id > ? [AND sandbox_id = ?] ORDER BY id LIMIT ?' returns the oldest rows first. Rows are never deleted (UPDATE/DELETE triggers), so once the limit is exceeded newer rows are only reachable by paging with after_id.
rows = box.audit.list(sandbox_id=sandbox_id, limit=5000): the oldest 5000 rows of that sandbox, no after_id. This is the fragment sandbox.html:19 re-requests every 3 s.

render(_audit.html, rows=rows[-400:][::-1], total=len(rows)) passes ids 4601-5000 and total 5000 (reproduced); newer rows, including gui_processes_stopped and gui_changes, are never rendered, and _audit.html:10 then prints the footer '최근 400개만 표시 (전체 5000개)'.

evidence.description: ' ORDER BY id LIMIT ?' is ascending, so any limit keeps the oldest rows; the same query serves the unpaged UI/CLI callers and the after_id paging API.
The UI takes the tail of the oldest-5000 window and reports total as len(rows), which cannot exceed 5000.
Footer '최근 {{ rows|length }}개만 표시 (전체 {{ total }}개)' (most recent N shown, total M) is false beyond 5000 rows; the harness printed '최근 400개만 표시 (전체 5000개)' with 5012 rows in the database.

cmd_audit requests /audit with limit=5000 and no after_id and prints everything it gets; there is no paging flag, and without --sandbox the query is system-wide. Real cmd_audit printed ids 1..5000 only.

GET /audit returns list(..., after_id=after_id, limit=min(limit, 5000)) with a default limit of 500: an unpaged call returns the oldest 500 rows (measured: newest id 500 of 5012); only after_id paging reaches newer rows, and neither the UI nor the CLI pages.
The sandbox page polls /ui/audit?sandbox_id=... on load, every 3 s and on audit-changed: this is the live oversight view, and its only other audit-related control is the verify button.
Every tool call appends tool_request here, policy_decision at line 305 and (when allowed and executed) tool_result at line 359: measured exactly 3 rows each for exec ls and list_dir.
default: allow, so list_dir, read_file, write_file and the GUI tools have no rule and need no approval; the read-only-exec allowlist (lines 25-27) allows ls, echo, cat and similar.

true and false are unquoted, so yaml.safe_load yields booleans and the allowlist holds 'True'/'False', not 'true'/'false'; measured: exec true returns 202 (approval requested), so the hunter's `exec true` example is wrong (the root cause is unaffected).

gui_changes (and gui_processes_stopped at line 225) are written only to the audit log and rendered only by web.py describe (line 62) and cli.py (line 280), so the two timelines are the only human-facing surface for them.
Documents the timeline as where the human sees the 'deleted: ...' list and the snapshot id for GUI-path changes; the README's known limitations do not mention a 5000-row cap.
The suite asserts that the /ui/audit page shows '삭제됨: old-report.md', confirming the timeline is the designed surface for gui_changes; no test brings a sandbox anywhere near the 5000-row limit.

conditions.description: Holder of the victim sandbox's agent token (prompt-injected agent). Rows can be created through the ordinary tool endpoints and MCP tools (list_dir, read_file, exec of an allowlisted command: 3 rows per call) or, with raw API access, by refused POST /approvals/{id} (1 row per call).

More than 5000 audit rows for the sandbox (sandbox page, `agentbox audit --sandbox`) or for the whole system (default `agentbox audit`). Agent-causable within minutes; long-lived ordinary sandboxes reach it too.
The human relies on the sandbox page timeline or `agentbox audit` output rather than paging GET /audit with after_id; the UI and CLI have no paging control.
Default policy (default: allow plus the read-only-exec allowlist) so list_dir, read_file, ls and echo need no approval. The refused-POST path does not depend on the policy.

execution.attacker_perspective: A prompt-injected agent holding its sandbox's agent token wants its later exec and GUI activity, and the gui_processes_stopped and gui_changes records the system writes about it, to stay out of the human's timeline; it first pads the audit table with cheap approval-free rows until the oldest-first window is full.
payloads: POST /approvals/apr_<n>  Authorization: Bearer <agent token of sb_v02>  body {"decision":"approve"}, repeated 4,991 times: each returns 403 and appends one approval_forbidden row tagged sb_v02; together with 9 rows from three probe tool calls the table holds exactly 5000 rows (ids 1..5000)

POST /sandboxes/sb_v02/tools/exec {"args":{"command":"echo AFTER_FLOOD_MARKER"}}; POST /sandboxes/sb_v02/tools/click {"args":{"x":10,"y":10}} (opens a GUI burst; the fake container then deletes /workspace/important.txt and leaves a background process, and the burst is aged 61 s); POST /sandboxes/sb_other/tools/exec {"args":{"command":"echo OTHER_SANDBOX_MARKER"}}: ids 5001-5012, including gui_processes_stopped 5008 and gui_changes 5009

Human side: GET /ui/audit?sandbox_id=sb_v02 with a browser-session cookie; the real cli.cmd_audit with sandbox=None, 'sb_v02' and 'sb_other'; GET /audit?after_id=5000&limit=5000 and GET /audit/verify with the human token
instructions: In sbx (no network, no Docker) run: sbx v02 /usr/bin/python3.13 -I -B /scratch/v02.py 5000 /scratch/v02.out (artifacts agents/v02/artifacts/v02.py and agents/v02/artifacts/v02.out; 512 MiB, 1 CPU, 64 pids, 120 s, uid 65534; about 17 s). It builds the real agentbox.api.build() app under a scratch AGENTBOX_HOME and replaces only SandboxManager (needs Docker) and fastapi.templating (jinja2 is not importable in sbx); the template stub records the context web.py passes and takes the footer text from the real _audit.html source line.

Step 0-1: with the sandbox's agent token send POST /approvals/apr_probe (403) and three probe tool calls (exec ls and list_dir are allowed and add 3 rows each; exec true returns 202 and needs approval), then 4,990 more refused POST /approvals/apr_N so the table holds exactly 5000 rows for sb_v02. Step 2: GET /ui/audit?sandbox_id=sb_v02 with a session cookie from box.desktop.new_session(): boundary control, the newest row (5000) is shown.

Step 3-4: as the agent run exec echo AFTER_FLOOD_MARKER and a GUI click (opens a GUI burst), alter the fake container (delete important.txt, leave a stray uid-1001 process), age the burst by 61 s, run an exec in an unrelated sandbox; poll /ui/audit again, which closes the burst so the real service code appends gui_processes_stopped and gui_changes. Inspect the template context and the unrelated sandbox's page.

Step 5-7: call the real cli.cmd_audit (default, --sandbox sb_v02, --sandbox sb_other) through a shim that injects the human token; GET /audit (default and after_id=5000) and /audit/verify; exercise the proposed remediation (newest-N plus COUNT(*) query, CLI after_id paging loop) on the same database.
execution.observed_result: With exactly 5000 rows the sandbox page showed ids 4601..5000 and the newest shown id equalled the newest in the database (boundary control). After 12 more rows (ids 5001-5012: exec and click tool_request/policy_decision/tool_result, snapshot 5006, gui_processes_stopped 5008, gui_changes 5009 for sb_v02; 5010-5012 for sb_other) the poll for sb_v02 returned status 200, template _audit.html, 400 rows, ids 4601..5000 (all approval_forbidden), total 5000, footer '최근 400개만 표시 (전체 5000개)', with no id above 5000, no gui_changes, no gui_processes_stopped and no AFTER_FLOOD_MARKER; the unrelated sb_other page still showed its own rows 5010-5012. Real cmd_audit printed 5000 lines, ids 1..5000, and none of the markers for both the default and --sandbox sb_v02; --sandbox sb_other printed ids 5010-5012. An unpaged GET /audit returned the oldest 500 rows (newest id 500). GET /audit?after_id=5000 returned ids 5001-5012 and /audit/verify returned ok=True over 5012 rows, so nothing is lost, only not shown. Proposed fix on the same database: the newest-400 plus COUNT(*) query returned ids 4610..5009 with total 5009 including gui_changes, and the CLI paging loop returned all 5012 rows. A second run gave identical numbers. Not executed: real Jinja2 rendering (unavailable in sbx), Docker-backed SandboxManager.

remediation.strategy: Make the human views read the newest rows and report the real total. Add AuditLog.recent(sandbox_id, limit) = SELECT COUNT(*) plus 'ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT ?' under the same lock, use it in web.audit_frag (newest first, matching the existing template), and make `agentbox audit` page /audit with after_id until an empty page (optionally add a --tail N flag or a newest-first /audit option so large logs are not transferred in full). Replace the same oldest-first pattern in web.verify_frag (web.py:270, limit=100000) with a point lookup of the broken id. Optionally add an index on audit(sandbox_id, id) for the filtered COUNT and reverse scans (CREATE INDEX does not conflict with the append-only triggers). Regression tests: append 5100 rows for one sandbox, assert GET /ui/audit renders id 5100 with total 5100 and that cmd_audit's fetch includes id 5100; assert the same for a sandbox filter when another sandbox holds most of the rows.

code_changes.fixed_code:
def recent(self, sandbox_id: str | None = None, limit: int = 400) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], int]:
        """Newest `limit` rows (newest first) and the real row count for the same filter."""
        where, args = (" WHERE sandbox_id = ?", [sandbox_id]) if sandbox_id else ("", [])
        with self._lock:
            total = self.conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM audit" + where, args).fetchone()[0]
            rows = self.conn.execute(
                "SELECT id, ts, sandbox_id, actor, event, tool, payload, prev_hash, hash FROM audit" + where
                + " ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT ?", args + [limit]).fetchall()
        return [
            {"id": r[0], "ts": r[1], "sandbox_id": r[2], "actor": r[3], "event": r[4], "tool": r[5],
             "payload": json.loads(r[6]), "prev_hash": r[7], "hash": r[8]}
            for r in rows
        ], total

likelihood.reason: No approval and no Docker work are needed: the rows come from the agent's own requests. In the harness 4,991 refused POST /approvals/{id} calls (one row each; needs raw API access with the agent token) took about 15 s in-process, and each allowed list_dir/read_file/exec of an allowlisted command adds exactly 3 rows (about 1,670 calls through the ordinary MCP tools, no raw API access needed). tool_concurrency (4 simultaneous) only slows this; there is no request-rate limit or row cap. Long-lived ordinary sandboxes cross 5000 rows without any attacker. It needs a human who relies on the timeline rather than paging /audit, and the frozen window stays visible (400 rows, constant total), so an attentive operator could notice that it stopped advancing.

impact.reason: Both human timelines (the sandbox page polled every 3 s, and `agentbox audit`) stop advancing while the UI footer claims to show the most recent rows, so later tool_request/tool_result, snapshot, takeover/handback, gui_processes_stopped and gui_changes rows are not shown. The README names the timeline as the way the human sees gui_changes, the compensating control for the ungated GUI path, so the lowest-trust principal can silence that control for itself at will. The default CLI is system-wide, so one sandbox's volume also hides other sandboxes' later events from `agentbox audit` without --sandbox; the per-sandbox UI window of an unrelated sandbox was not affected (checked). Bounded: no row is lost or altered (GET /audit?after_id= returns them, verify passes), the approval queue, snapshots, stray-process kill and tool gating are unaffected, and there is no disclosure or privilege gain.

confidence.reason: Reproduced twice with identical numbers through the real api.build() app: agent-token HTTP requests created the rows, the real service.py code wrote gui_processes_stopped and gui_changes, and the real web.py audit_frag route and real cli.cmd_audit ran. Only Docker (SandboxManager) and Jinja2 rendering were stubbed, and the footer text came from the real _audit.html line. The boundary control (exactly 5000 rows shows the newest row), the unrelated-sandbox control and the paging/verify checks support the causal reading, and the ordering, the limit, the missing paging and the absence of any documented cap are direct from source. The hunters' artifacts (h-audit, h-wild) agree.
